title: Berlin Districts - FAQ
subtitle: Which Bezirk you live in, what it runs, and which errands skip it.

items.q: How many districts does Berlin have?
items.a: Berlin has **12 districts** (Bezirke) since 1 January 2001. They were formed from **23** older districts and are divided into **97 Ortsteile**, the localities most people name when they say where they live.

items.q: Which Berlin districts were merged in 2001?
items.a: Nine of today's districts are mergers: Mitte (with Tiergarten and Wedding), Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, Pankow (with Prenzlauer Berg and Weißensee), Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, Steglitz-Zehlendorf, Tempelhof-Schöneberg, Treptow-Köpenick, Marzahn-Hellersdorf and Lichtenberg (with Hohenschönhausen). **Spandau, Neukölln and Reinickendorf** kept their borders.

items.q: Do I have to register at the Bürgeramt of my own district?
items.a: No. You can register your address at **any Bürgeramt in Berlin**, and the same goes for ID cards and passports. If your district has no free appointments, search the whole city.

items.q: Is the Ausländerbehörde run by my district?
items.a: No. Residence permits are handled by the **Landesamt für Einwanderung**, one state office for all of Berlin, whichever district you live in.

items.q: Who do I call about noise or a car blocking my driveway?
items.a: The **Ordnungsamt of the district where it happens**, which is not always your own. Most districts take reports online through Ordnungsamt-Online.

items.q: Can EU citizens vote in Berlin district elections?
items.a: Yes. EU citizens registered in Berlin can vote for the **Bezirksverordnetenversammlung**, the district assembly, which is elected on the same day as the Berlin parliament. Voting for the Abgeordnetenhaus itself needs German citizenship.
